translatorNotes: Register: informal tú, consistent with Phase 1.

'RFQ' (Request for Quote) kept as the acronym (widely used in ES industrial procurement); glossed as 'solicitud(es) de cotización (RFQ)' on first use in title/schema/FAQ. FLAG: some ES/LatAm buyers say 'pedido de cotización' or 'presupuesto' — reviewer to confirm.

'quote' -> 'cotización'; 'estimator' -> 'estimador'; 'shop' (machine/fab shop) -> 'taller'; 'shop floor' -> 'planta'; 'front office' -> 'oficina'; 'purchase order' -> 'orden de compra'; 'supplier chase' -> 'seguimiento/persecución a proveedores'; 'lead time'/'delivery date' -> 'fecha de entrega'; 'specs' -> 'especificaciones'; 'drawing' -> 'plano'; 'planners/schedulers' -> 'planificadores/programadores'.
'where is my order' rendered as '¿dónde está mi pedido?' (matches the ecommerce page). 'ERP' kept.
Stat chip data-prefix 'under ' -> 'menos de ' and suffix ' sec' -> ' seg'; '20+ hrs' -> '20+ h'; '24/7' unchanged.
Prices/figures unchanged, currency named: '$1,000 and $5,000' -> '1.000 y 5.000 dólares'; '$50 to $300' -> '50 a 300 dólares'; 'six figure ERP' -> 'ERP de seis cifras'.
Case study reuses the real-estate brokerage speed story (source does too, framed as speed-to-quote analogy); kept faithful.
'QuickBooks' kept. Other brands (n8n, Make, Zapier, Twilio, Google Workspace, Slack) unchanged.
Blog 'related reading' links point to English blog posts (Phase 3 not started); anchor text translated. Nav/footer service + industry links point to /es.
